*I didn't expect anything else. I climbed over into the back toward her. She made no attempts at eye contact.*
Yang: "I don't regret running away from Ruka's world."
Li-Fang: "..."
*Ruka's world... and my mother's world... She had spent her whole life filling that world with her works. I rejected it. Not only that, I had taken my mother away from it in the lofty name of a life elsewhere. My mother saw nothing interesting here.*
Yang: "Hey, there are places I want to go with you."
Yang: "I want to go to the Topqap Palace with you... It's a famous museum in Istanbul. And there are more."
Yang: "We have to go see the Taj Mahal, right? And Angkor Wat, and..."
Li-Fang: "I'll go with you."
*Yang: "Y? I did not expect that answer. I looked into her eyes.*
Yang: "Where will you go with me?"
Li-Fang: "Wherever you want."
Yang: "Really..."
*My mother looked very exhausted, but also at peace. I put my hand on my mother's, atop her knees.*
Yang: "We'll stay together now."
Li-Fang: "..."
*I pressed my mother's hand. I saw wrinkles in her skin that spoke of her age and conveyed to me the unvarnished truth that this truly was my mother. I left my mother in the car and went outside. My first steps in the outside world were on concrete, stained brown with dirt and age. I smelled the clean air of the countryside even through the pungent smell of gasoline.*
Riko: "Yang."
Yang: "Oh, Riko. What is it?"
Riko: "Jay is buying something to drink for everyone. He sent me to ask what you and Gramma want."
Yang: "I don't need anything."
Riko: "But..."
Yang: "I'm fine, but ask Gramma. She's in the car."
Riko: "Okay."
*Riko nodded and ran to the car. Her skirt fluttered in the wind.*
Jay: "Yang, is Mina still not back?"
*Jay had finished smoking and came up to me.*
Yang: "Mina isn't here... Why?"
Jay: "That's odd. She went to the restroom with Jessica. I can't find her."
Yang: "Maybe they're taking turns. Maybe she needs a little time."
Jay: "Maybe..."
*We leaned against the car, waiting for Mina and Jessica to return. Cars seldom passed us, and in their stead little tree sparrows sometimes came down to investigate, but their little beaks fruitlessly picked at the concrete and they flew off again.*
Jay: "Mina is taking forever."
Yang: "You're right."
*Hajiro Mina..._n never came back.*
Li-Fang: "That's why I said we shouldn't leave her world."
Yang: "Huh?"
Li-Fang: "You should have known. She cannot leave her world."
Yang: "Mother, are you..."
*She was serious.*
Li-Fang: "I told you. I only wanted to protect her."
My mother looked out toward the vast and bright sky as though that was where she expected to find Mina.
